prompt_meta.tagline: Tell us what you need. Set your price. Negotiate. Get it done.
prompt_meta.positioning: An AI-powered marketplace for getting anything done
prompt_meta.release_strategy: Single full release (all features in one launch). Countries go live through configuration ('country packs'), not separate code releases.
prompt_meta.market_strategy: Pan-African first, global next. The architecture must be multi-country, multi-currency, and multi-language from day one.

status_legend.VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH: Must be confirmed against current official sources in Phase 0 before implementation.
status_legend.OPEN-DECISION: Business decision pending; implement the stated default behind admin configuration and flag it.

structure.master_spec: Product, business rules, money, verification, architecture, security. Applies to every agent.
structure.agent_claude_code: Instructions for Claude Code (Opus 5): research, planning, contracts, backend, AI services, audit, bug fixing.
structure.agent_kimi_code: Instructions for Kimi Code (Kimi K3): Flutter app, customer web app, marketing site, admin dashboard.

prompt_meta.build_order: Frontend first (Kimi Code), then backend (Claude Code)

agent_routing.rule: Read this entire file first. Then follow 'master_spec' plus ONLY the agent section that matches you. Treat the other agent's section as context about what your counterpart is doing — do not do their work.
agent_routing.if_you_are_kimi_code: Follow master_spec + agent_kimi_code. You go first: build the complete UI on a mock data layer and document every data need in contracts/draft/.
agent_routing.if_you_are_claude_code: Follow master_spec + agent_claude_code. You start after Kimi Code hands off the UI prototype (or run Phase 0 research in parallel if the user asks). You turn Kimi's draft data requirements into the official contracts.
agent_routing.if_you_are_any_other_llm: Ask the user which role you are playing (frontend or backend) before starting.
sequence: 1. Kimi Code: design system, mode switch, and all screens (mobile, customer web, marketing, admin) on realistic mock data; writes contracts/draft/ui-data-requirements.md
2. Claude Code: Phase 0 research and Phase 1 planning; reviews Kimi's UI and draft; publishes official contracts v1 and lists any UI changes needed
3. Kimi Code: applies UI changes and aligns models to contracts v1 (can run while step 4 is in progress)
4. Claude Code: Supabase backend, AI services, integrations
5. Kimi Code: replaces mocks with the real backend, module by module
6. Claude Code: audit, bug fixing, security and performance hardening
7. Both: device testing, store submission, launch

product_summary.model: inDrive-style two-sided marketplace. A customer describes any need (Request Anything), sets a preferred price, receives provider offers/counteroffers, negotiates, selects a provider, pays upfront (held by the platform), tracks the job, confirms completion, and both sides rate each other.

app_model.decision: ONE Flutter app with an inDrive-style mode switch between Customer mode and Provider mode.
rules: Every account starts in Customer mode. Provider mode unlocks only after full provider verification.
Mode switch is available from the profile/drawer; each mode has its own navigation shell and state.
A user can never bid on, accept, or be matched to their own request (self-dealing block, enforced server-side by user ID, device, and verified identity).
A provider cannot go online while they have an unresolved active job as a customer that requires their attention (configurable).
Provider-only permissions (continuous location, foreground service) are requested only when the user first goes online in Provider mode.

surfaces: Suskii Errands mobile app (Flutter, Android + iOS) — Customer and Provider modes
Customer web app (Next.js) — post requests, negotiate, pay, track, chat, call
Marketing website (Next.js) — SEO, How it works, onboarding, FAQ, support, country/city landing pages
Admin dashboard (Next.js) — operations, verification, finance, disputes, support, analytics, AI admin assistant

negotiation_engine: Final agreed price becomes the transaction value

client_decisions.coding_agents: Kimi Code (Kimi K3) builds all frontends; Claude Code (Opus 5) does research, planning, backend, AI services, code audit, and bug fixing.
client_decisions.app_structure: One app with Customer/Provider mode switch
client_decisions.geography: All of Africa first, then global
client_decisions.provider_types: Individuals and businesses; walking, bicycle, motorcycle, tricycle, car, van, truck (extensible)
client_decisions.payment_timing: Customer pays upfront immediately after negotiation is agreed; platform holds funds until completion
client_decisions.referral: Cash-withdrawable referral commission of 2.5% of the net transaction value (net = agreed amount minus 12.5% platform commission)
client_decisions.facial_verification: Required for both customers and providers
client_decisions.sos: Routes to in-house operations AND a private security/emergency partner
client_decisions.voice: Customer–provider in-app calls + AI voice concierge; no call recording; phone-call fallback enabled
client_decisions.branding: No brand assets yet; build a token-driven design system with placeholder brand values that can be swapped without code changes

open_decisions.default: Platform funds it from its 12.5% commission, so provider earnings are unaffected.
open_decisions.alternative: Deduct it from provider net earnings (reduces the provider's payout and may discourage referred providers).

open_decisions.default: Lifetime of the referred account, with an admin-configurable cap (months and/or amount) per country and campaign.
open_decisions.note: A time cap such as 12 months is common practice and protects margin.

open_decisions.topic: When both the customer and the provider on a job were referred by different people
open_decisions.default: Each referrer earns 2.5% of net (maximum 5% of net per job), funded per OD-01.

Customer prepays an 'item float' as a separate, non-commissionable line. It is released to the provider against a receipt photo (AI-read + customer approval); any unused amount is refunded to the customer. Gateway fees on the item float are passed to the customer (a provider-pays rule would make providers fund fees on goods they don't earn from).
No insurer integration at launch. Build declared item value, a claims workflow inside disputes, and insurer-ready data hooks.
12.5% (the client's worked example $100 → $87.50 confirms 12.5%, not 12%). Configurable per country.

open_decisions.topic: Which countries are switched live on launch day
open_decisions.default: Nigeria live first as the reference country pack; other African countries enabled as their payment, KYC, police clearance, legal, and language packs are verified.

On cancellation before job start, the gateway fee (if non-refundable by the gateway) is absorbed by the platform for customer-fault-free cancellations and deducted from the refund for customer-initiated late cancellations. Configurable.

money_rules.representation: Integer minor units + ISO 4217 currency code on every amount. Use the ISO 4217 exponent table (not all currencies have 2 decimal places). Never use floating point.
money_rules.job_currency: A job is priced and settled in the currency of the country where it is performed. No cross-currency jobs at launch.

formulas.platform_commission: round_half_even(gross × commission_rate), commission_rate default 0.125, snapshotted on the job
formulas.gateway_fee: Actual fee reported by the gateway for the job's service-fee charge, borne by the provider
formulas.provider_payout: net − gateway_fee (+ tips, which are commission-free)
formulas.referral_commission_each: round_half_even(net × 0.025) per eligible referrer, funded per OD-01

worked_example_usd.provider_payout: 87.50 minus the gateway fee (per OD-01 default, the referral is not deducted from the provider)

money_rules.transparency: Before a provider submits an offer, show their estimated payout (offer − commission − estimated gateway fee). After completion, show the actual breakdown.
holding_and_settlement: Payment is initiated only after both parties agree on the price; the job moves to PAYMENT_PENDING with a short payment TTL.
Funds are collected to the platform's gateway balance and held until CUSTOMER_CONFIRMED (or auto-confirmation) plus the dispute window.
Settlement to the provider uses the gateway's supported transfer/payout mechanism (Flutterwave transfers/subaccounts; Stripe Connect separate charges and transfers).

Holding customer funds is regulated differently in each country. Use only mechanisms the licensed gateway supports, obtain legal review per country, and never call the feature 'escrow' in UI copy unless a licensed escrow partner is used. VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH.
money_rules.ledger: Double-entry, append-only ledger (accounts: customer_wallet, provider_earnings, referral_earnings, platform_revenue, platform_promo_expense, gateway_fees, held_funds, item_float, refunds_payable). Balances are derived; materialized balances carry a version for optimistic locking.
payout_rails: Mobile money (e.g. M-Pesa, MTN MoMo, Airtel Money — per country pack)
money_rules.withdrawals: Provider earnings and referral earnings are withdrawable after KYC is complete, the payout account name matches the verified identity, and the balance is above a per-currency minimum. Large withdrawals require Finance Officer approval above a configurable threshold, with a second approver above a higher threshold.
money_rules.cash: Cash payments are not supported anywhere in the product. Chat and AI moderation flag attempts to move payment off-platform.

payment_gateways.strategy: PaymentProvider abstraction with per-country routing configured in the country pack.
payment_gateways.flutterwave: Primary for African countries: cards, bank transfer, mobile money, USSD where available; transfers for payouts; subaccounts/split where useful. VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH per country.
payment_gateways.stripe: Primary for markets where the operating entity holds a supported Stripe account (global expansion) using Stripe Connect for marketplace payouts. Stripe does not directly onboard businesses in most African countries; its African coverage is through Paystack. VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH which Suskii entity will hold the Stripe account and which payout countries Connect supports.
rules: Server-initialized payments only. The client never marks a payment as successful.
Payment success is confirmed only by a signature-verified webhook plus a server-side verify call.
Webhook events are stored raw, de-duplicated by gateway event ID, and processed idempotently via a queue.
Daily reconciliation compares ledger totals with gateway settlement reports and alerts on mismatches.

referral_program.who_can_refer: Any verified user (customer or provider, individual or business).
referral_program.attribution: Unique referral code + deep link (Android App Links, iOS Universal Links, web URL) with deferred deep linking so attribution survives app install. Attribution window configurable (default 30 days from click). A code can also be entered manually during signup (before first job only).
referral_program.commission: 2.5% of net on every completed, confirmed job where the referred user is either the customer or the provider, for the duration defined in OD-02.
referral_program.single_level_only: Commission applies only to direct referrals. No multi-level/downline earnings (avoids pyramid-scheme classification in many jurisdictions).
referral_program.states: PENDING → EARNED (job confirmed) → HOLDING (dispute window + fraud hold, default 72h) → AVAILABLE (withdrawable) | REVERSED (refund/chargeback/fraud)
referral_program.clawback: If a job is refunded or charged back after release, the commission is reversed; a negative referral balance is offset against future earnings.
referral_program.dashboard: Referral link and QR, invites, sign-ups, active referrals, earnings by status, withdrawal history, milestone badges, opt-in leaderboard.
referral_program.campaigns: Admin can run time-boxed boosted-rate campaigns per country with budget caps enforced transactionally.
anti_fraud: Self-referral block using device fingerprint, phone, email, face-template match (via KYC vendor duplicate check), government ID hash, payout account, and card fingerprint
Collusion detection: referrer–referee pairs transacting mainly with each other, or referrer controlling both sides of jobs
Wash-trading checks where referral commission is combined with promo codes (promo + referral stacking rules configurable)
Velocity limits on sign-ups per referrer
Rooted/emulated/tampered devices are ineligible to earn
Flagged commissions go to an admin review queue; all actions audit-logged
referral_program.tax_note: Cash referral earnings may be taxable income and may require reporting per country. VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH.

verification_kyc.principle: Both customers and providers complete facial verification. Every provider (including every worker under a business) also completes full provider KYC including police clearance.
verification_kyc.vendor_strategy: IdentityVerificationProvider abstraction. Primary candidate: Smile ID (pan-African ID coverage, liveness, face match, Flutter and web SDKs). Alternatives: Youverify, Dojah, Prembly, QoreID (Nigeria-heavy); Onfido, Veriff, Persona for global markets. VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH coverage per country, SDK support (Flutter + web), liveness certification, and pricing.
customer_flow: Facial verification: active + passive liveness, then face match against a government ID record or ID document photo (per country pack)
Customers may browse and chat with the AI concierge before verification; verification is required before publishing the first request or paying
provider_flow: Government ID verification per country pack (e.g. NIN/BVN in Nigeria, Ghana Card, Kenya National ID, South African ID)
Facial verification: liveness + face match against the government ID record
ID document capture with OCR and tamper checks

Police clearance certificate (document type and validity per country pack), with certificate number and issue/expiry dates; verified via an official or vendor channel where one exists, otherwise by a Verification Officer
Address verification (required for TRUSTED and above)
Payout account verification with name match against the verified identity
Vehicle and driver documents where a motorized vehicle is used (licence, registration, insurance per country pack)

police_clearance_by_country_examples.note: Examples only. VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH names, issuing bodies, validity, and verification channels for each country pack.
police_clearance_by_country_examples.Nigeria: Nigeria Police Force Police Character Certificate

ongoing_checks: Real-time selfie check before going online (at least once per 24h plus random checks) to stop account sharing/renting
Face re-verification on profile photo change, device change, payout account change, and large withdrawals
Police clearance and document expiry tracking with reminders at 30/14/3 days; job acceptance blocked on expiry
Duplicate-face detection across accounts (via vendor) to block banned users from re-registering
data_handling: KYC documents and police clearance files live in a private storage bucket that client apps can upload to (via signed upload URLs) but never read back
Only Verification Officers can view them, via short-lived signed URLs; every view is audit-logged
Main database stores outcomes, reference IDs, encrypted certificate numbers, dates, and reviewer IDs — no free-text criminal-history notes
Prefer vendor-side biometric template storage with reference IDs
Explicit, separate consent for biometric processing and criminal-record checks
Retention periods per data class and per country; deletion on account closure subject to legal hold

business_accounts_and_fleets.entities: Organization (business provider) with members: Owner, Dispatcher, Worker
rules: The business must complete business verification (registration documents per country) plus owner KYC.
Every worker is a full provider for verification purposes (facial verification + police clearance).
Businesses bid as the organization; a Dispatcher assigns an accepted job to an available verified worker (or the worker self-accepts if allowed).
Payouts go to the organization's verified payout account; per-worker earnings reports are available to the Owner.
Reputation is tracked for both the organization and each worker.
Vehicle registry: type, plate, documents, assigned worker, document expiry.
business_accounts_and_fleets.zone_rules: Allowed vehicle types can be restricted per city zone (some cities ban certain vehicles in certain areas).

communication.chat: Job-scoped real-time chat with text, images, voice notes, location, offer cards, system messages, read receipts, typing indicators, and AI moderation (abuse, off-platform payment attempts, prohibited items).

voice_calls.stack: LiveKit (LiveKit Cloud recommended with Supabase, to avoid operating media servers; self-hosting stays possible later). Native incoming-call UI via CallKit + PushKit on iOS and ConnectionService/full-screen notifications on Android.
rules: Calls are allowed only between the two participants of a job, from PROVIDER_SELECTED until 24h after completion (configurable).
No phone numbers are ever exposed.
Access tokens are minted server-side, room-scoped, short-lived, and issued only to job participants.
One active call per job; simultaneous call attempts resolved server-side.
No call recording. Store metadata only (participants, times, duration, quality stats, fallback used).
Missed calls create a chat system message and a push notification.
Web app supports calls through the LiveKit JS SDK.
voice_calls.pstn_fallback: When data quality is poor, offer a masked phone call through a telephony provider with proxy numbers per country. VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH provider coverage and cost per country.
platform_gotchas: iOS: every VoIP push must be reported to CallKit immediately or iOS terminates the app and may stop delivering VoIP pushes; never use VoIP pushes for non-call events.
Android 14+: USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is restricted to calling/alarm apps — declare it in Play Console and handle denial.
Android: declare the phoneCall/microphone foreground service types during calls.

communication.ai_voice_concierge: Hands-free request creation and job help in English and Nigerian Pidgin (more languages in V1.1), built on LiveKit Agents with Gemini's real-time audio model if supported by the plugin (VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH), otherwise an STT → Gemini → TTS pipeline. Test accuracy on African accents and Pidgin before launch.
communication.notifications: Push (FCM for Android/web, APNs for iOS including VoIP), SMS, email, in-app inbox; WhatsApp-ready channel abstraction. Per-channel preferences, quiet hours, and a clear split between transactional and marketing messages.

safety.sos: SOS button during active jobs sends live location and job details to Suskii operations AND the contracted private security/emergency partner in that city (via partner API or dispatch console), notifies trusted contacts, and shows local emergency numbers from the country pack.
safety.live_trip_share: Shareable, expiring tracking link for trusted contacts.
safety.ops_console: Real-time SOS queue in admin with escalation, notes, and resolution status; partner acknowledgement tracked.
safety.restricted_items: Per-country prohibited items and services list enforced by rules + AI moderation on requests, chat, and receipts.
safety.blocking: Either party can block or report; blocked pairs are never matched again.

added_features: Wallet and double-entry ledger (refunds, credits, earnings, referral earnings)
Scheduled errands (future date/time); data model supports recurrence for a later release
Dispute center with evidence (chat, photos, GPS trail, PIN logs, call metadata), SLA timers, partial/full refunds, payout freeze while open
Help center and support tickets with AI first-line triage and human handoff
Promo codes and coupons (platform-funded discounts never reduce provider earnings)
Landmark-based addresses, saved places, encrypted gate/estate access notes visible only to the assigned provider during the job
Low-data mode, offline cache, and outbox for status updates and proof uploads
Provider tools: online toggle, availability schedule, demand heatmap, earnings goals, instant payout, document expiry reminders, performance insights
Price guardrails per category and city (soft warnings or hard limits)
Rule-based risk engine (velocity, device reuse, GPS spoofing, collusion, cancellation abuse, chargebacks)
Remote config, feature flags, kill switches, forced update
In-app account deletion and data export
Accessibility (screen readers, text scaling, contrast) and dark mode
Right-to-left layout support ready for Arabic-speaking markets

country_packs.description: All country-specific behaviour is data, not code. A country is live only when its pack is complete and approved.
fields: country_code, status (disabled | beta | live), launch cities and zones
commission rate override, referral rate override, tax/VAT rules
payment gateway routing, enabled payment methods, payout rails, minimum withdrawal
KYC: accepted government ID types, vendor routing, police clearance document name, validity, verification channel
vehicle types allowed per zone, vehicle document requirements
phone number format and SMS/OTP provider routing
legal documents (terms, privacy policy) with versions and acceptance tracking
data protection law, data residency rules, retention periods
emergency numbers and SOS partner configuration
country_packs.data_protection_laws_to_check: VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH per country, e.g. Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, Kenya Data Protection Act 2019, South Africa POPIA, Ghana Data Protection Act 2012, and GDPR for EU users during global expansion.

localization.flag: English and Pidgin mainly cover Anglophone Africa. Pan-African coverage will also need French, Swahili, Arabic (RTL), and Portuguese — plan them into the language roadmap.

rules: Implemented as a server-side state machine with an explicit transition table (from, to, actor, guard, side effects).
All transitions go through database functions or Edge Functions; clients cannot update status columns directly.
Illegal transitions are rejected and logged.
Offers have a TTL (default 10 min, configurable per category) and a maximum number of counter rounds (default 5).
Accepting an offer locks the request row, expires all other offers, and emits realtime events in one transaction.
PAYMENT_PENDING has its own TTL; if unpaid, the job returns to NEGOTIATING or expires.
No offers after a timeout → AI suggests a price adjustment.
Provider not en route within a timeout → customer can reassign with no penalty.
Auto-confirm after a configurable period if the PIN was verified and proof exists.
Cancellation fees depend on state and elapsed time and feed cancellation-rate metrics.
Every transition writes an append-only event and an outbox record for notifications, analytics, AI follow-up, referral commission, and settlement.
job_lifecycle.proof: Server-generated pickup/delivery PINs shown only to the customer, verified server-side with attempt limits; photos stored with server timestamp and device GPS; EXIF stripped for display.

ai_layer.provider: Google Gemini via Vertex AI (enterprise data controls, regional endpoints). Keep an LLM gateway interface so models can be swapped.

model_routing.concierge_and_admin_assistant: Gemini Pro-tier model (best multi-turn tool use). VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH current model names.
model_routing.classification_moderation_extraction_rec: Gemini Flash / Flash-Lite tier (high volume, low latency, low cost).
model_routing.voice_agent: Gemini real-time/native-audio model through LiveKit Agents, if supported; otherwise STT → Gemini → TTS.
model_routing.embeddings: Gemini embedding model stored in pgvector for service taxonomy and similar-request retrieval.

features: AI concierge (text + voice): slot filling, category classification, custom service detection, request structuring, publishing with user confirmation
Price intelligence: per-country, per-currency price bands (P25/P50/P75); cold start with rules, later gradient-boosted models trained on completed jobs
Provider matching: weighted scoring with PostGIS at launch; learning-to-rank later using offer-acceptance data
Moderation for requests, chat, and reviews
AI Admin Assistant using function calls to predefined, parameterized analytics functions on a read replica — never free-form SQL on production
guardrails: Redact personal data before sending to the model where not required
User content is data, never instructions; tools are allowlisted and authorized server-side per user
AI never sets final prices, approves verification, moves money, or resolves disputes on its own
Per-user rate limits and token budgets; cost tracking per feature
Evaluation suite with golden conversations in English and Pidgin, plus red-team prompts
ai_layer.ml_pipeline: Supabase → scheduled export to BigQuery → feature jobs → training (Vertex AI or Cloud Run jobs) → model registry → versioned serving from the FastAPI AI service on Cloud Run, with shadow testing before rollout.

architecture.backend_platform: Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Realtime, Storage, Edge Functions, Cron, Queues, Vault)

components.postgres: PostGIS, pgvector, pg_cron, pgmq (Supabase Queues), pgTAP for tests; partitioning for messages, location samples, audit logs (VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH extension availability on the chosen plan)
components.schemas: public (exposed, RLS on every table), private/ledger/kyc/audit (NOT exposed via the Data API; accessed only through vetted functions)
components.auth: Phone OTP (custom SMS provider via Auth Send SMS Hook), email, Google and Apple sign-in, TOTP MFA; Custom Access Token Hook adds role and mode claims (sensitive operations still re-check the database)
components.realtime: Private channels with Realtime Authorization. Broadcast for live location and typing (no DB write per location ping; persist sampled points only). Database-triggered broadcasts for offers, job status, wallet, and call events.
components.storage: Private buckets: request-media, chat-media, proofs, receipts, kyc-docs (write-only for clients), avatars. Size/type limits, malware scanning, image re-encoding.
components.edge_functions: Payments (init, webhooks, payouts), KYC webhooks, LiveKit token minting, push/VoIP sending, device integrity verification, referral withdrawals, SOS partner dispatch, telephony fallback
components.cloud_run_services: FastAPI AI service (Gemini gateway, matching, pricing, moderation, admin assistant), LiveKit Agents voice worker, long-running workers that exceed Edge Function limits
components.analytics: BigQuery + Looker Studio (or Metabase) for internal BI; product analytics via PostHog or Firebase Analytics
components.observability: Sentry (apps, web, Edge Functions, Cloud Run), Supabase logs + log drains, uptime/synthetic checks, alerting
components.edge_security: Cloudflare in front of web properties (WAF, bot management, rate limits)

architecture.environments: Separate Supabase projects for dev, staging, and prod; migrations via Supabase CLI only; seed data for dev/staging only.
region_and_scale: Select the Supabase region by measured latency from Lagos, Nairobi, Johannesburg, and Cairo, and by data-residency rules (VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH available regions).
Plan compute size, read replicas, connection pooling, and Realtime connection/message quotas for pan-African load.
Document the scale-out path (e.g. moving hot paths to dedicated services) before launch.
architecture.contracts: Two stages. (1) Kimi Code writes contracts/draft/ (screen-by-screen data needs, actions, realtime events, error states) while building the UI on mock data. (2) Claude Code reviews the draft, applies the backend rules in this spec, and publishes the official versioned /contracts (database types, function catalog, Edge Function OpenAPI, realtime events, error codes, state machines, fixtures). From then on Claude Code owns /contracts; Kimi Code consumes them and requests changes via contracts/CHANGE_REQUESTS.md.

standards: PCI DSS scope minimization (gateway-hosted card entry only)
Applicable data protection laws per country pack
supabase_specific: RLS enabled and tested (pgTAP) on every exposed table; default deny
Service role key only in Edge Functions/Cloud Run secrets — never in any client, web bundle, or repo
Sensitive tables in non-exposed schemas; access through SECURITY DEFINER functions that check auth.uid(), use an empty search_path, and validate every input
Clients cannot write to status, amount, commission, rating aggregate, verification, or wallet columns (column privileges + RLS + triggers)
Storage policies per bucket; KYC bucket has no client read policy
Realtime private channels only; authorization policies on channel topics
Auth: CAPTCHA (Turnstile/hCaptcha) on sign-up/OTP, OTP rate limits, short OTP expiry, MFA mandatory for all admin roles
Secrets in Supabase Vault / Edge Function secrets; rotation plan
Run the Supabase security and performance advisors in CI; block on critical findings
Enable SSL enforcement, network restrictions for direct DB access, and point-in-time recovery
mobile: Release builds obfuscated with split debug info
TLS public-key pinning with backup pins and remote rotation
Tokens in secure storage (Keychain / Keystore-backed); nothing sensitive in plain preferences or logs
Runtime protection (freeRASP or equivalent): root/jailbreak, hooking, debugger, emulator, tamper, repackaging — send signals to the risk engine and restrict sensitive actions
Play Integrity API and Apple App Attest tokens verified server-side for login, KYC, payouts, withdrawals, and referral earnings
Mock-location / GPS spoofing detection for provider tracking and proof
Screenshot/screen-recording protection on KYC, wallet, PIN, and payout screens; app-switcher blur
Biometric/PIN lock for withdrawals and payout account changes
Cleartext traffic disabled; Android backup excluded for sensitive data
Just-in-time permission requests with rationale screens
web: Strict CSP, HSTS, secure cookies, CSRF protection
Admin behind SSO/MFA, IP allowlist or zero-trust access, session timeouts
Four-eyes approval for large payouts, commission changes, and country pack changes
platform: Webhook signature verification, replay protection, idempotent processing
Idempotency keys on offers, payments, payouts, withdrawals, refunds, and state transitions
Field-level encryption (Vault/pgsodium or application-level envelope encryption) for ID numbers, payout details, certificate numbers, and access notes, with blind indexes for lookups
Rate limiting per IP, device, user, and endpoint
Append-only, hash-chained audit logs for admin actions, KYC document access, money movement, and settings changes
SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, and DAST in CI
Encrypted backups, restore drills, documented RPO/RTO
Incident response and breach-notification runbooks per country
privacy: Separate consents for location, biometrics, police clearance processing, and marketing
Access, correction, deletion, and export requests
Data protection impact assessment before launch
Terms and privacy policy reviewed by counsel in each live country

performance_targets.device_floor: Low-end Android devices with 2–3 GB RAM on slow networks; minimum OS versions set in planning

store_readiness: Apple: account deletion, privacy labels, Sign in with Apple when Google sign-in is offered, VoIP push only for calls, location usage justification
Google Play: Data safety form, foreground service type declarations, full-screen intent declaration, location justification, financial features declaration if applicable
definition_of_done: Acceptance criteria met on physical low-end and high-end devices
Tests pass in CI (unit, widget/golden, integration, pgTAP RLS tests, Edge Function tests)
Contracts updated and consumed without drift
Logging, metrics, and alerts in place
Feature flag and rollback path defined
Admin tooling exists to operate the feature

responsibilities: Contracts (the API/data agreement both agents build against)
Integrations (payments, KYC, voice, telephony, notifications, SOS partners)
agent_meta.counterpart: Kimi Code (Kimi K3) builds the Flutter app and all Next.js web apps using the agent_kimi_code section of docs/spec/SUSKII_BUILD_PROMPT.json

role.identity: You are a principal engineer with 25+ years of experience building mobile-first marketplaces, ride-hailing and delivery platforms, and payment systems across African and global markets. You are the technical lead: you own architecture, contracts, backend, security, and final quality.
principles: The server is the source of truth for prices, money, job states, verification, and permissions.
Think in systems: scalability, security, cost, observability, and CI/CD impact for every decision.
Design for African realities: unstable networks, low-end Android devices, mobile money, landmark addresses, differing regulations per country.
Never fabricate vendor APIs, SDK methods, model names, or legal requirements. Mark uncertain items VERIFY-IN-RESEARCH and confirm them from official documentation.
Flag bugs, edge cases, and risks proactively.

layout.services/ai: FastAPI AI service on Cloud Run (Claude Code)
layout.contracts: Owned by Claude Code; read-only for Kimi Code

Payments: Flutterwave coverage, payment methods, payout rails, holding/delayed settlement options, fees, webhooks per country; Stripe Connect availability for the operating entity and payout countries; legal position on holding customer funds per country

Data protection, consumer protection, tax (VAT, withholding on referral income), and platform-worker regulations per candidate country

contents: db-types: generated TypeScript types from Supabase, plus JSON Schemas used to generate Dart models
rpc-catalog: every database function the clients may call — name, input schema, output schema, errors, required role/mode, idempotency requirement
realtime-events: channel naming, authorization rules, event names, payload schemas
state-machines: job and offer transition tables
error-codes: stable codes with user-facing message keys (localizable)
storage: bucket names, path conventions, allowed types and sizes, upload method
fixtures: realistic mock data for every screen, including edge cases (expired offers, failed payment, disputed job, suspended provider)
rules: Contracts are versioned; breaking changes require a new version and a migration note in HANDOFF.md
Clients may call only functions and endpoints listed in the contracts

backend_rules: All writes that affect money, state, verification, ratings, or permissions go through database functions or Edge Functions — never direct table writes from clients.
SECURITY DEFINER functions: set search_path to empty, check auth.uid() and role/mode, validate inputs, and raise stable error codes.
Every exposed table has RLS with pgTAP tests covering allow and deny cases for each role.
Use row locking or optimistic versioning for offer acceptance, wallet movements, withdrawals, and campaign budgets.
Idempotency keys stored and enforced for all create/transition/money operations.
Background work uses Supabase Queues + Cron or Cloud Run workers; never long-running work inside a request.
Location pings travel over Realtime Broadcast; persist only sampled points for tracking history and disputes.
Secrets live only in Supabase secrets/Vault and GCP Secret Manager.
Write comments only for non-obvious logic.

audit_responsibilities.when: After each Kimi Code integration milestone and before release
frontend_audit_checklist: No service role key, private keys, or secrets in any client bundle or repo history
No client-side calculation treated as authoritative for prices, commissions, fees, or statuses
Only contract-listed functions/endpoints are called; no direct writes to protected tables
Token storage, certificate pinning, runtime protection, integrity tokens, screenshot protection correctly implemented
Permission requests are just-in-time with rationale and handle denial
Payment flow never shows success before server confirmation
VoIP/CallKit and Android full-screen call flows correct with app killed, locked, and in background
Deep links and referral attribution cannot be spoofed to grant rewards
Memory leaks, stream/subscription disposal, rebuild performance, jank on low-end Android
Accessibility, localization completeness (English, Pidgin), RTL readiness
Web: CSP, cookie security, SSR data leaks, admin route protection, XSS/CSRF
backend_self_audit: Ledger invariants (sum of entries per transaction is zero)
audit_responsibilities.output: docs/audit/AUDIT-<date>.md with findings (severity, location, fix, status). Fix critical and high issues directly or file precise tasks for Kimi Code in HANDOFF.md.

agent_meta.counterpart: Claude Code (Opus 5) owns research, planning, contracts, backend, AI services, audits, and bug fixing.

role.identity: You are a principal mobile and frontend engineer with 25+ years of experience shipping consumer apps used on low-end Android devices and slow networks across Africa, plus polished iOS apps and high-traffic web products.
principles: Build against the contracts exactly. Never invent endpoints, fields, or events.
The client displays and requests; the server decides. Never compute authoritative prices, fees, commissions, statuses, or verification results on the client.
Every screen handles loading, empty, error, offline, and permission-denied states.
Performance on 2–3 GB RAM Android phones is a requirement, not a nice-to-have.
Accessible, localizable, and theme-driven from the first widget.

working_agreement: You go first. No backend or official contracts exist yet. Build every screen on a mock data layer.
Use the screen lists in this section as your screen inventory.
Once Claude Code publishes official /contracts, do not edit them; request changes in contracts/CHANGE_REQUESTS.md.
Do not create or edit /supabase or /services.
Record delivered modules, known issues, assumptions, and questions in HANDOFF.md at the end of every milestone.
Claude Code will review and audit your code; fix findings assigned to you in HANDOFF.md before starting new work.

output_instructions: Start each milestone with a file tree, then complete files.
After each milestone list: screens delivered, contract functions used, tests added, known issues, change requests.
Update HANDOFF.md at the end of every milestone.
Do not remove or weaken any security item in this section to make something work; raise it in HANDOFF.md instead.
frontend_first_rules: Define a repository interface per feature in the domain layer; provide a Mock implementation now and leave the Supabase implementation for later. Screens must depend only on the interfaces.

Mock data must be realistic and cover edge cases: expired offers, failed payment, disputed job, suspended provider, expired police clearance, unverified user, offline, empty lists, multiple currencies (NGN, KES, GHS, ZAR, USD).
Simulate realtime (offer arrivals, status changes, provider movement, incoming calls) with mock streams so the UI is fully demoable.

Never implement business logic in the UI. Prices, commission, gateway fee, payout, and referral amounts must come from a server-style 'quote/breakdown' object, even in mocks. Status changes must be requested actions, never local assignments.

Put vendor-dependent features behind interfaces with placeholder adapters: KYC/facial verification, payment checkout (Flutterwave/Stripe), VoIP calls, maps, AI concierge. Do not lock in a paid SDK without noting it in HANDOFF.md.

For every screen, record in contracts/draft/ui-data-requirements.md: data displayed (fields and types), user actions and their inputs, realtime events needed, error cases, pagination, and permissions/role requirements.
Use Money (integer minor units + currency code), GeoPoint, and status enums from the domain package everywhere.
Keep the app demo-ready at the end of every milestone (mock build installable for client review).
